dedupe_keys.name: fao fapda policy database of national food and agriculture policy decisions

description: The FAPDA policy database holds more than 18,000 national policy decisions and 3,000 national policy frameworks on food security, nutrition and agriculture for over 150 countries. Each entry is verified, linked to its source document and classified; policy decisions are grouped as consumer-oriented measures such as cash transfers, food assistance and price controls, producer-oriented measures such as minimum prices and input subsidies, and trade and macroeconomic measures such as tariffs and export controls, following a classification based on FAO's 2008 guide on responding to high food prices. It is maintained by the FAPDA team of the Food and Agriculture Organization, which collects information from FAO country and regional offices and online sources. Coverage is global. The database is available online free of charge, with a user guide and classification document to download; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: coverage depends on what FAO staff and online sources report, and the page gives no start year or update schedule. For simulation it documents government responses such as export bans, price controls and support payments, useful for modelling how policy reactions amplify or damp food supply shocks after droughts, conflicts or trade disruptions. It is related to the WTO and ADB Trade in Critical Minerals record in this catalogue, which likewise pairs trade flows with policy measures for another sector.
